description: Implement nonce-based CSP to remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src (Issue #1070, primary XSS win), with a single source of truth for the CSP. Per-request nonce is generated in proxy.ts (Next 16 middleware), injected into BOTH the incoming request header 'content-security-policy' (so Next 16 app-render applies nonce= to its hydration/framework/injected scripts) AND the response header (for browser enforcement), plus a custom x-nonce header. First-party server-component inline <style> tags (tenant branding) receive the nonce via headers() as defense-in-depth. style-src 'unsafe-inline' is RETAINED with a documented rationale (next/font + react-hot-toast inline style attrs + tenant branding make full style-src removal fragile and a UI-regression risk); this is the deliberate, defensible partial per the issue's 'nonces or hashes' guidance and correctness-over-completeness. This is ONE coherent feature: change proxy.ts, next.config.mjs, nginx.conf, the branding style components, add a test, and update docs.
steps: In proxy.ts: add a helper to generate a per-request nonce with `Buffer.from(globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()).toString('base64')` (or `crypto.getRandomValues` -> base64). The nonce charset must match Next's regex /^'nonce-([A-Za-z0-9+/_-]+={0,2})'$/.

In proxy.ts: build the CSP string dynamically per request. Base directives MUST match the current production policy EXACTLY except script-src: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-<NONCE>'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' ws: wss:; frame-ancestors 'none'; frame-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:. In dev (NODE_ENV !== 'production') add 'unsafe-eval' to script-src (React refresh). Do NOT weaken any other directive.

In proxy.ts: apply the CSP only to HTML page navigations (non-API GET requests), NOT to /api/ responses, and skip prefetch/RSC requests where sensible. The existing matcher already excludes _next/static and static assets. Set the nonce on the forwarded REQUEST headers and return NextResponse.next({ request: { headers: <cloned req headers with 'content-security-policy' set> } }); then set 'content-security-policy' and 'x-nonce' on the returned response headers too. Preserve ALL existing proxy behavior (auth redirect, rate limiting, CSRF, CORS, x-request-id) — the nonce/CSP must be layered on the existing NextResponse.next() paths for page requests without altering the API/auth logic.

In next.config.mjs: remove the static Content-Security-Policy header from async headers() for page routes so there is ONE source of truth (proxy.ts) and no conflicting/duplicate CSP. Keep all OTHER headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, cache-control blocks) unchanged. Update the code comment to point at proxy.ts as the CSP source and note style-src retention rationale + #1070.

In nginx.conf: remove the duplicate `add_header Content-Security-Policy ...` line (it carries unsafe-inline for script-src and would either double-set or override the app's per-request header, defeating the nonce). Add a comment that the app now emits a per-request nonce-based CSP and nginx must NOT set or strip Content-Security-Policy. Leave the other nginx add_header security headers intact.

In components/branding/branding-provider.tsx and components/shared/branded-header.tsx (both server components): read the nonce via `const nonce = (await headers()).get('x-nonce') ?? undefined;` (make the component async if needed) and pass `nonce={nonce}` to the <style> element as defense-in-depth. If making branded-header.tsx async is impractical where it's used, leave it and document; branding-provider.tsx is the primary tenant-wide one. Do NOT change the sanitization of the CSS content.

Add tests/unit/csp-nonce.test.ts following the tests/unit/proxy.test.ts mocking pattern (mock next/server, jose, csrf, rate-limit-edge). Assert: (a) a page GET response has a Content-Security-Policy header containing "script-src 'self' 'nonce-" and NOT containing "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'"; (b) the response carries an x-nonce header whose value appears inside the CSP script-src as 'nonce-<value>'; (c) two separate requests get different nonces; (d) the CSP still contains the unchanged hardened directives (object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', frame-ancestors 'none', worker-src 'self' blob:, connect-src ... ws: wss:); (e) /api/ responses are NOT given the page CSP header. Also add a file-content assertion in this test (or extend security-hardening.test.ts) that next.config.mjs no longer contains "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'" and nginx.conf no longer contains a script-src unsafe-inline CSP line.

Update DEPLOYMENT.md (and docs/SECURITY-ANALYSIS.md CSP row if quick) to describe: the new nonce-based CSP posture, that script-src 'unsafe-inline' was REMOVED via per-request nonce in proxy.ts, that style-src 'unsafe-inline' is RETAINED-with-rationale (list the blockers: next/font, react-hot-toast inline style attributes, tenant branding <style>) plus a documented follow-up path (style nonce/hash migration), and the OPERATOR DEPENDENCY that nginx (and any CDN/WAF) must NOT set, strip, or override the Content-Security-Policy header now that the app emits it per-request.
acceptance_criteria: Production CSP emitted for HTML page navigations contains script-src 'self' 'nonce-<base64>' and does NOT contain 'unsafe-inline' in script-src
No duplicate/conflicting CSP header remains (next.config.mjs page CSP removed; nginx.conf CSP line removed); proxy.ts is the single source
Nonce is per-request (different across two requests) and the same value is present in both the CSP script-src and the x-nonce response header
All other CSP directives are byte-for-byte equivalent to the prior hardened policy (no directive weakened)
First-party tenant-branding <style> in branding-provider.tsx receives nonce={nonce} from the x-nonce header
New tests in tests/unit/csp-nonce.test.ts pass and would fail if unsafe-inline were reintroduced to script-src
DEPLOYMENT.md documents the new posture, the style-src retention rationale, and the nginx/CDN must-not-override operator dependency
verification: npx vitest run tests/unit/csp-nonce.test.ts tests/unit/proxy.test.ts tests/unit/security-hardening.test.ts

Manual (document, cannot run live host here): load a tenant page in a browser, open devtools console, confirm NO 'Refused to execute inline script'/'violates CSP' errors, confirm hydration works (interactive UI), styles render, react-hot-toast toasts render, realtime websocket connects, Sentry initializes. Confirm response header Content-Security-Policy has script-src with nonce and matches the nonce on Next's injected <script nonce=...> tags in the HTML.
